Women vs Thailand Women 20th Match, Group B India tour of New Zealand, 2026 Santner out of India Tests with fractured hand; Foxcroft called up
 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet [File photo] Mitchell Santner was struck on the back of his right hand in the fifth ODI against India © AFP [File photo] Mitchell Santner was struck on the back of his right hand in the fifth ODI against India © AFP All-rounder Mitchell Santner has been ruled out of the upcoming two-Test series against India with a fracture in his right hand. Santner, New Zealand’s white-ball captain, sustained the injury during the fifth ODI against India in Mount Maunganui on Sunday (November 15), copping a blow to his right hand while batting.
 Santner was tended to by the physio during the 37th over of New Zealand’s chase after being struck on the back of his right hand by an Arshdeep Singh delivery. While he continued to bat and was eventually dismissed for 24, scans have revealed a fracture that will rule him out of the Tests.
 A New Zealand Cricket statement said that his return-to-play time is “being worked through”, while his involvement for the four-Test tour of Australia in December will be “updated in due course”.
 All-rounder Dean Foxcroft has been called up in Santner’s place for the Tests in Wellington and Christchurch. Foxcroft, who played the last two ODIs against India, has featured in a lone Test, scoring 98 against Ireland in May earlier this year. He displayed excellent form in the unofficial Tests against India A, with scores of 51, 42, 93 and 10*.
 New Zealand will face India in the first Test at the Basin Reserve starting November 19, before the second Test commences at the Hagley Oval in Christchurch on November 27.
